effective.basis: Old state: UDE official card rulings (Sangan/Witch: 'If you have no eligible monsters, your opponent gets to see your Deck to verify', captured 2005-06-16) through Konami's own per-set rulings documents - Machina Mayhem (2010-04-06, 18 days before the Edison snapshot), Starstrike Blast (2010-11-16), Storm of Ragnarok (2011-02-02). New state: KDE-US Tournament Policy section 'Card/Hand/Deck Verification' forbids verifying the opponent's Deck (first located capture 2019-04-03; still current in v2.5, 2025-09-05). No dated announcement of the change was found, so the interval 2011-02-02 .. 2019-04-03 stays open.

changes.historical_text: When this card is sent from the field to the Graveyard, each player selects 1 Level 3 or lower Normal Monster from their Deck, and adds it to their hand after showing it to the opponent. The Decks are then shuffled.
changes.summary: Period procedure, not a text erratum: in upstream's pre-errata script a player who adds no monster reveals their entire Deck to the opponent (Duel.GetFieldGroup(tp,LOCATION_DECK,0) followed by Duel.ConfirmCards), where the modern script confirms only a card that was actually added and reveals nothing on a whiff. Everything else resolves identically - a mandatory trigger (EFFECT_TYPE_SINGLE+EFFECT_TYPE_TRIGGER_F) on EVENT_TO_GRAVE from the field, each player picking a Level 3 or lower Normal Monster out of their own Deck, and activation unconditionally legal in both (the target function returns true without checking the Deck), so only the failed-search verification procedure differs.

review.notes: Packet conflict: upstream's pre-errata cdb text ('If this card is sent from the field to the Graveyard: Each player adds 1 Level 3 or lower Normal Monster from their Deck to their hand. Each player who didn't add a monster to their hand must reveal their Deck to their opponent.') matches no printed English version. It is the modern v2 sentence with 'When' swapped for 'If' and a prose reconstruction of the era verification ruling appended; the matcher lands on v1 at ratio 0.7294. No English printing ever carried the reveal sentence, and the If/When distinction is not implemented either way - both scripts are plain EFFECT_TYPE_TRIGGER_F on EVENT_TO_GRAVE with no EFFECT_FLAG_DELAY. Note also that the activation-condition question the shared brief separates out (whether the card can be used with no valid target) does not arise here: both scripts always activate, so this is procedure (A) only and the shared chronology applies cleanly. The chain is started at v1 (DR2-EN189, 2005-10-20), the text in force across the Edison snapshot. Earlier: v0 (AST-076, 2004-06-01), in force at the GOAT snapshot, differs from v1 only in pronouns (his/her -> their). Trailing: v1 -> v2 (LCYW-EN255, 2012-09-29) is PSCT dropping the 'after showing it to the opponent. The Decks are then shuffled.' procedural wording - cosmetic, and the modern script still performs the reveal of the added card.
